uncited: Transformer-based Reconstruction methods replace the iterative optimization loop of standard 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) with a feed-forward neural network that directly predicts Gaussian parameters from input images [S1, unofficial].
This approach solves the computational bottleneck of per-scene optimization, enabling real-time reconstruction from single or sparse views.

It differs from iterative siblings by eliminating the need for gradient descent on scene parameters, instead relying on learned priors within the transformer architecture to generalize across scenes [S1, unofficial].
**Tokenization**: Input data (images and/or camera poses) is encoded into a sequence of feature tokens.
Images are typically processed by a Vision Transformer (ViT) backbone [S1, unofficial].
Camera parameters (intrinsics and extrinsics) are encoded into separate token embeddings [S1, unofficial].

**Transformer Processing**: The concatenated token sequence is processed by a transformer encoder/decoder to model spatial and geometric relationships between views and the 3D scene structure [S1, unofficial].

**Direct Parameter Prediction**: The network decodes the transformer output directly into 3D Gaussian attributes: mean position $\mu$, covariance $\Sigma$ (or rotation $R$ and scale $S$), color $c$, and opacity $\alpha$ [S1, unofficial].
**Differentiable Rendering**: The predicted Gaussians are rendered using standard differentiable rasterization to produce an output image [S1, unofficial].
**Training Objective**: The network is trained end-to-end using photometric losses (e.g., LPIPS, SSIM) between the rendered output and ground truth images [S1, unofficial].
The family originates from the need to accelerate 3D Gaussian Splatting, which traditionally requires per-scene optimization [S1, unofficial].
Large Reconstruction Model (LRM) introduced the transformer-based feed-forward approach for 3D reconstruction [S1, unofficial].
GS-LRM and Flash3D adapted this paradigm specifically for 3DGS, with GS-LRM focusing on sparse multi-view inputs and Flash3D on monocular depth estimation [S1][S2, unofficial].
Reconstruction-based Generation extends this by integrating diffusion-based multi-view synthesis [S1, S2].
